{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABipL_Ww", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhL_v2o", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 87, "title": "Remove bundled samples and align mute controls and tab-visibility playback with snes-rust", "body": "## Problem

The screen-first UI from #85 / PR #86 is now implemented. Three follow-up simplifications are desired.

1. The emulator is sufficiently developed that publicly bundled samples are no longer needed. The sample catalog, sample programs, downloadable diagnostics and demo-only distribution/build logic create unnecessary UI, maintenance and licensing overhead.
2. The toolbar still uses a text-based Enable audio / Mute audio / Resume audio button, unlike the maintainer's snes-rust player, which uses a speaker/mute icon and a volume slider.
3. The current frame loop already gates execution on `!paused && !document.hidden`, and its visibilitychange handler persists saves, clears timing debt, releases keys and flushes audio. However, it does not explicitly synchronize the effective running/suspended status or retry suspended audio on visibility restoration, and restart paths can advance a frame outside that gate. Make visibility suspension and manual pause distinct, predictable states consistent with the reference player's behavior.

## Expected outcome

Simplify the player and match the interaction conventions of snes-rust:

- Remove **all public bundled sample content** from the current browser app and production distribution: plustaker, YOKO, the MSX2 diagnostic demo, Weave disk demo, BASIC example / Graphics demo / Sound demo starter buttons, sample listings and downloadable diagnostic/sample ROM/DSK/CAS links. Remove obsolete catalog/assets, demo-only code, UI, metadata and documentation from the current tree as applicable. No backward compatibility for removed sample URLs, catalog entries or demo-specific behavior is required; no replacement bundled samples.
- Keep a clean local-media-only workflow. Preserve independently authored **test-only** fixtures and their source where needed to verify real hardware, file import, boot, audio, rendering and regression behavior, but do not ship them in the public Pages artifact or expose them in the UI. Retain actual emulator firmware, required runtime resources, and their applicable license/provenance notices. This is not a request to rewrite Git history or remove license notices for code/assets still in use.
- Replace the visible Enable audio / Mute audio / Resume audio text button with the same accessible speaker / muted-speaker icon pattern as snes-rust, next to the existing volume slider. Use a coherent mute/volume state, preserve the last nonzero volume, and respect browser autoplay restrictions without requiring a separate enable-audio text button.
- Separate the user's requested Play/Pause state from effective playback. If the document becomes hidden while playing, automatically suspend emulation and audio; when visible again, automatically resume **only if play was still requested**. A manual Pause must remain paused after any hide/show sequence. Match snes-rust's relevant interaction behavior, without importing unrelated SNES functionality.

## Context and reproduction

- Baseline MSX main: `ca1e8d0b60d142fcbfae8c07014454aee3d18ca0`; [PR #86](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/86), [Issue #85](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/85), [successful Pages run](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/45512375852).
- MSX app: https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/. `web/index.html` exposes bundled cartridge demos, disk demo, BASIC starters and diagnostic download links. `web/app.js` contains `loadCatalog`, `demoChoice`, `playDemo`, `mount-disk-demo` and starter handlers; `scripts/build.sh` copies `demos/` and generates fixtures into dist; `scripts/check-dist.mjs` requires the samples and their links. Remove obsolete dependencies coherently.
- Audio currently has `audioEnabled`, `audioContext`, `outputGain` and the `audio` button's textual states; `volume` already adjusts the output gain. `frame()` stops advancing emulation while document.hidden, but `updateStatus()` and the toolbar use only the manual paused flag. Review all state transitions including async media loads and explicit restarts.
- Reference: https://takahirox.github.io/snes-rust/; pinned revision `3ee93a124f266312a84a4d2ef464c94f4660d110`: [web/index.html](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3ee93a124f266312a84a4d2ef464c94f4660d110/web/index.html), [web/app.js](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/3ee93a124f266312a84a4d2ef464c94f4660d110/web/app.js). Its mute button has inline speaker SVG with sound waves or mute mark, accessible Mute/Unmute state, a volume slider, last nonzero level, a shared gain stage and local audio preference. Its `playRequested`, `running`, `syncPlayback()` and visibilitychange handler distinguish manual pause and visibility suspension. The user specifically wants these conventions. Use the reference as a design/behavior reference, not an instruction to add persistent personal ROM storage or bundled SNES demos.
- Before implementation, inspect the current checkout and actual reference sources; do not assume the published app or reference app matches historical documentation exactly.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Remove public samples completely

- [ ] Delete the public sample catalog and third-party demo assets/associated now-unused notices from the current tree (including `demos/` and related exclusively demo-specific code, tests, assets and references). Remove the disk demo insertion/download, BASIC starter actions/listings, public diagnostic downloads and now-unused demo-only UI/style/handlers/manifest fetching/ABI paths. Remove obsolete sample-only files and documentation; retain historical development evidence where needed to accurately document past work rather than rewriting history. No redirects, compatibility shims, placeholder sample menus or replacement samples.
- [ ] Split test fixture generation from production packaging as needed. The production Pages artifact must contain only the functioning app, actual required firmware/resources and applicable notices, with no bundled sample ROM/DSK/CAS, diagnostic download or sample catalog. Validate exact distribution inventory and no sample fetches/links at runtime. Test-only fixtures remain independently authored, legal and generated/served locally for automated tests; never reintroduce them as publicly offered media. Retain runtime firmware including C-BIOS and the original disk boot environment, and any necessary diagnostic loader functionality rather than deleting working emulation features just because their public sample is removed.
- [ ] Simplify Cartridge, Drive A: and Cassette insertion paths to local files (retain meaningful mount/read-only/boot/rewind/eject/export settings and safety warnings; unnecessary single-choice menus may be removed). Preserve local ROM/DSK/CAS validation, mapper selection, firmware policy, cancellation/same-file retry and atomic session preservation, SRAM and modified-disk safeguards, MSX2 Weave BASIC and Retro CRT defaults. Keep necessary operational help and legitimate copyright/licensing notices. Do not remove functional support for these media or the BASIC language.
- [ ] Remove assertions whose sole purpose was verifying removed public demo functionality. Retain meaningful independent hardware/real-Wasm/browser regressions by migrating to original local test fixtures as needed; avoid redundant tests or retaining public demos just to satisfy obsolete selectors. In particular, test local cartridge, disk and tape loading, relevant model/mapper/firmware behavior, saves, audio and CRT without depending on the removed public samples. No proprietary assets required.

### Audio interaction parity

- [ ] Replace the visible audio text button with an inline speaker icon with sound waves when audible/unmuted and a clear muted icon when muted. Use an accessible button name (Mute/Unmute or appropriate retry description), keyboard operability, pressed state and concise nonblocking status for blocked/suspended audio; keep screen focus behavior predictable. Do not use a separate text-based Enable audio/Resume audio button, decorative icon with no behavior, or claim audio is playing while the context is blocked.
- [ ] Keep a single shared browser gain stage. The icon toggles mute and restores the last nonzero volume; setting the slider to zero reflects mute, and a positive value unmutes/updates gain, including currently queued sources. Match the reference's lightweight local audio preference (volume and last nonzero level only), with robust defaults if storage is invalid or unavailable. The emulator sound chip/PCM state must remain independent of the browser output volume.
- [ ] Start or resume AudioContext only as allowed by browser user gestures; use relevant deliberate gestures such as unmute, adjusting volume, Play/Resume, Reset and media insertion where appropriate. Keep user mute across visibility changes; if an unmuted context is suspended, attempt recovery where permitted and leave an actionable icon/status if blocked. Do not autoplay without permission, reset the emulator for audio changes, accumulate unbounded audio sources or introduce stale sound after pause/mute.

### Visibility and pause parity

- [ ] Maintain manual playback intent separately from effective running state. Running + hidden becomes auto-suspended; visible + still requested play becomes running again. Manual Pause + hidden + visible remains paused. Repeated hide/show, tab backgrounding during startup or asynchronous media/firmware imports, and explicit manual commands must not accidentally override intent or duplicate execution. Use Page Visibility API, not ordinary focus loss alone (clicking Settings/Help or a file picker must not count as a hidden tab). Preserve normal deliberate Reset/boot behavior when visible and define its interaction with hidden state; do not let hidden completion of an import or startup advance unsolicited frames or falsely show running.
- [ ] While hidden or explicitly paused, stop normal CPU/VDP/audio/media-time advancement, flush queued audio, release held keyboard/joystick inputs, persist relevant existing saves and discard stale timing debt. On automatic resume restart the scheduler from fresh time without catching up hidden elapsed time or replaying audio, and do not reassert held keys. Keep paused CRT/Clean redraw behavior independent of emulation. Reflect effective Running/Paused/auto-suspended status and manual control intent accurately; a manually paused session must not resume simply because visibility changes.
- [ ] Add focused automated real-Wasm Chromium tests for the four requested transitions (running→hidden→visible, paused→hidden→visible), repeated transitions, frame/time and audio cessation/continuation, input release, hidden async import/startup and muted/unmuted/suspended audio behavior. Use observable independent state/frame/audio evidence, not just button labels; use real visibility transitions when reliably available or controlled visibility instrumentation for deterministic lifecycle tests, documenting limitations. Also test the icon/slider/accessibility/blocked-audio retry behavior, no public sample assets or requests, and representative local ROM/disk/tape workflows at both local root and Pages prefix. Reuse existing tests/fixtures and follow repository CI performance principles; do not add unnecessary cross-product coverage or unrelated CI changes.
- [ ] Update README, Help and runtime messages to describe local-only media, the speaker/mute control, volume and the auto-suspend/resume semantics. Keep distribution and applicable license/provenance checks accurate. Run configured applicable checks (`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test`, `git diff --check`) and report actual results. Follow the English Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → revision → merge/close lifecycle. No subjective human approval, proprietary ROMs or physical device required.

## Optional validation

The maintainer may compare the MSX and SNES players in their own browser using legally obtained local media. Manual listening and physical-device testing are optional.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After successful merge and Pages deployment, check the actual published site at https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/: no sample menus/buttons/downloads or requests for removed assets; MSX2 BASIC starts, the speaker icon and volume control work, and changing tabs suspends and resumes a running session but never resumes a manually paused session. Use a private local original test fixture if needed, not a newly published sample. Record the deployed revision, Actions run, environment, observed results and any blocked/unperformed checks. Close the source Issue on merge; pending post-merge-only checks do not block approval or require reopening. Track actual defects in linked follow-up Issues after checking for duplicates.
